one_liner: Header-only flat red-black tree map/set in a vector; 1.4-1.9x faster than std::map at scale.
what_it_does: dro::FlatMap and dro::FlatSet are STL-compatible red-black tree map/set implementations that store nodes contiguously in a std::vector instead of individually heap-allocating each node. The API mirrors std::map/std::set (at, operator[], find, insert, erase, lower_bound, iterators) so it's close to drop-in, but keys and values must be default-constructible and erased slots aren't freed until shrink_to_fit() or destruction.
how_it_is_fast: Storing nodes in a vector keeps the tree cache-contiguous and lets the implementation prefetch the next probed level during binary search on insert/erase, cutting cache misses versus a pointer-chasing red-black tree. Rotations swap node and child slots in place rather than relocating via pointers, and erase swaps the deleted key with the in-order successor then moves it to the vector's end instead of freeing/reallocating a node.
when_to_use: Insert/find/erase-heavy workloads on int32-like keys where std::map's per-node allocation dominates, especially at 1M-10M elements (1.4-1.9x measured gain).
You can pick a MaxSize index type (uint8_t-uint64_t) matching your expected element count for space efficiency.
Keys/values are default-constructible and you don't need pointer/reference stability across inserts/erases.
You want ordered iteration plus a map-like API without accepting flat_map's insert/erase cost.
when_not_to_use: Find-dominated workloads at large sizes: boost::flat_map find is faster than dro::FlatMap by 1M elements (134ns vs 234ns), and folly::heap_vector_map overtakes dro on find from ~100K elements.
Code that holds iterators across modifying operations: every insert/erase/clear invalidates ALL iterators, not just erased ones.
Long-lived containers with heavy erase churn: erased slots stay allocated until shrink_to_fit() or destruction, so memory can grow unbounded between compactions.
Production use requiring maturity: project is self-labeled Beta Testing with ~50% test coverage and has no issue-tracker history to gauge stability (issue tracker is empty).

integration.min_toolchain: C++20 per README; repo's own CMakeLists.txt builds with C++23
integration.platforms: not documented (no architecture-specific intrinsics in the header; no platform restrictions stated)
integration.drop_in_for_baseline: partial — API mirrors std::map/std::set (at, operator[], find, insert, erase, iterators) but requires default-constructible key/value, invalidates all iterators on any modification, and doesn't auto-deallocate erased slots

gotchas: All iterators are invalidated by any modifying operation (insert/erase/clear/swap), not just iterators to erased elements as in std::map.
erase() does not free memory; call shrink_to_fit() or destroy the container to reclaim space from erased slots.
Key and Value types must be default-constructible in addition to copy/move-assignable.
The MaxSize template parameter (an integral type) bounds max_size() and throws std::runtime_error if the container grows past it.
pick_this_over_siblings_when: Pick over boost::container::flat_set/flat_map when insert/erase throughput matters more than find at scale (boost::flat_map degrades sharply on insert/erase, e.g. 146,200ns at 1M vs dro's 283ns), but pick boost::flat_map instead if find dominates. Versus fast-containers or frozenca/BTree (larger, more mature B-tree alternatives with wider verified gains), dro::FlatMap is a smaller header-only option but is explicitly beta with ~50% test coverage.
verified_claims_summary: On gcc 14.2.1 with libstdc++, -DCMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=Release, on an isolcpus-pinned Intel Core i5-9300H (4 cores), dro::FlatMap beat std::map at 10,000,000 int32 elements: insert 622ns vs 855ns, find 551ns vs 774ns, erase 627ns vs 916ns (~1.4-1.9x across sizes); numbers are from the repo's committed benchmarks/results/*.txt, not chart-reading.
